name: LAN9514I-JZX
title: USB 2.0 hub with four downstream ports and 10/100 Ethernet controller
summary: The LAN9514 joins a four-port Hi-Speed USB 2.0 hub and a 10/100 Ethernet MAC with PHY in one 64-pin QFN, so one upstream USB link gives a system four USB ports and a wired network port. It runs from a single 3.3 V supply with on-chip 1.8 V regulators and one 25 MHz crystal, and an optional serial EEPROM sets its MAC address, descriptors and hub options. LAN9514 covers 0 to +70 °C, LAN9514i -40 to +85 °C.
key_figures: 288 mA typ, 100BASE-TX full duplex, USB high speed

circuits.title: Power connections
circuits.description: One 3.3 V rail feeds the five VDD33IO pins directly, each with its own 0.1 µF capacitor to ground. A 120 Ω (at 100 MHz, 2.0 A) ferrite bead FB1 splits off the analog rail for the seven VDD33A pins, again with 0.1 µF at each pin. The internal core regulator delivers 1.8 V on the two VDD18CORE pins, which are joined and held up by 4.7 µF and two 0.1 µF. The internal USB PLL regulator, fed from VDD33A, puts 1.8 V on VDD18USBPLL (1.0 µF); a second identical bead FB2 carries it to VDD18ETHPLL, which has 0.1 µF. The exposed pad is the ground.

circuits.title: Port power control with USB power switches
circuits.description: Each downstream port has its own USB power switch running from 5 V. The port's PRTCTL pin drives the switch enable and also listens to the switch's active-low over-current flag on the same wire: the hub turns power off by pulling the line low, and turns it on by releasing it to its internal pull-up, so the switch's open-drain fault output can pull it low and the Schmitt input sees the fault. The switch output powers the attached USB device.

circuits.title: Port power control with poly fuses
circuits.description: Each port's VBUS comes from 5 V through its own poly fuse. A diode runs from the PRTCTL pin (anode) to the fused VBUS (cathode). With power enabled, the pin's internal pull-up holds the anode near 3.3 V. When the fuse trips, VBUS falls to 0 V, the diode pulls the pin to about 0.7 V, and the input reads that low as over-current. Driving the pin low to disable power has no effect on VBUS, since the diode blocks it.

circuits.title: Ganged port power control with one poly fuse
circuits.description: One poly fuse from 5 V powers every downstream device. For ganged control all four PRTCTL pins are tied together and meet the anode of a single diode whose cathode sits on the fused supply.

circuits.title: Output equivalent test load
circuits.description: Output timing is specified into 25 pF from the output to ground.

operation.text: A Hi-Speed USB 2.0 hub with one upstream and four downstream ports, every port with its own integrated PHY, plus a 10/100 Ethernet MAC and PHY hung on the hub's internal port 1, an EEPROM controller and a JTAG TAP controller. The Ethernet controller is reported to the host as a non-removable device on the hub.

The hub meets USB 2.0 and enumerates in one of two ways: full-speed only, or high-speed capable (falling back to full speed). Downstream it serves low-, full- and, when running high speed, high-speed devices. Each downstream port has a dedicated transaction translator for mixed-speed traffic. VBUS to the downstream ports is switched, current-limited and fault-sensed by external USB power switches. Series terminations and all D+/D- pull-ups and pull-downs are integrated, the over-current inputs have internal pull-ups, and the USB data pins are internally protected against shorts.

PortMap reorders or disables downstream ports in any sequence, renumbering the remaining ports to match the host's numbering. PortSwap exchanges D+ and D- per port so a pair meets its connector without crossing. PHYBoost raises the USB drive strength in four steps (+4, +8, +12%) to recover signal quality lost to layout or long cables. A port can be declared to carry a permanently attached device.

The integrated MAC and PHY meet IEEE 802.3 10BASE-T and 802.3u 100BASE-TX, with auto-negotiation, full or half duplex with flow control, automatic polarity correction, HP Auto-MDIX and energy detect. Toward USB it presents four endpoints (control, interrupt, and a bulk pair: bulk-in carries received frames, bulk-out frames to send); vendor commands give access to its statistics and its control and status registers. Further features: 32-bit CRC generation and checking, padding insertion and removal, TCP/UDP checksum offload, loop-back, address filtering by one exact 48-bit address or a 64-entry multicast hash, pass-all-multicast, promiscuous and inverse filtering. A USB remote wakeup can be raised by Wake on LAN, by a Magic Packet, or by a change of link status.

Three USB suspend states trade wakeup sources against power. SUSPEND0 stops the MAC and other internal clocks and keeps GPIO, Wake on LAN and Magic Packet wakeup. SUSPEND1 draws less and keeps GPIO and link-status-change wakeup. SUSPEND2, the default, keeps only GPIO wakeup. Every GPIO can be a remote wakeup source while suspended.

All supplies are 3.3 V (VDD33IO for the I/O, VDD33A for the analog sections); an internal regulator makes the 1.8 V core supply on VDD18CORE, and a second internal regulator makes the 1.8 V USB PLL supply. Both VDD18CORE pins must be joined. The exposed pad is ground and must be connected. Bus-powered and self-powered operation are both supported.
A built-in power-on reset needs no external reset parts. nRESET is optional; if driven, it must stay low for at least 1 μS. POR, nRESET, USB reset and software reset (SRST) trigger an EEPROM load.

One 25 MHz source clocks both USB and Ethernet: a parallel-resonant fundamental-mode crystal (the preferred choice) with matched load capacitors on XI and XO, or a single-ended 25 MHz oscillator of +/- 50ppm driving XI with a nominal 0-3.3V swing and XO left open. The driven clock's duty cycle is 40% min, 50% typ, 60% max. The load capacitors are chosen from the crystal's load capacitance, the 3 pF XI and XO pin capacitance and the board capacitance. CLK24_OUT can supply a 24 MHz reference to a partner hub when CLK24_EN enables it.
USBRBIAS takes a 12K 1.0% resistor to ground, setting the high-speed transmit current and termination impedance. EXRES takes a 12.4K 1.0% resistor to ground for the PHY's bias circuits.

PRTCTL2 to PRTCTL5 each combine a port's power enable with its over-current sense. To remove power the pin drives low and its pull-up is switched off to save power. To apply power the driver turns off and the pull-up turns on, leaving an open-drain line that an external switch's open-drain fault output can pull low; the Schmitt input then reads over-current. A filter rides out transients such as low voltage while the part powers up. Used with a poly fuse, each pin needs an external diode to its fused VBUS. For ganged control all four PRTCTL pins are tied together.
The hub connects (enables its USBDP0 pull-up) according to VBUS_DET, a 5 V tolerant input. A bus-powered hub ties it to VDD33IO, as does a self-powered hub permanently attached to its host.

An optional 3-wire 93C46-type EEPROM, 2K/4K bits organised 256/512 x 8, holds the MAC address, USB descriptors and the hub configuration; nine address bits are used. After reset the controller reads address 0: 0xA5 means a configured EEPROM and the contents are loaded, anything else leaves the hardware defaults in place. POR and nRESET load both hub and Ethernet settings; a USB reset reloads only the MAC address; SRST or an EEPROM reload command reloads only the Ethernet controller's settings. No USB transactions are accepted until loading finishes. Without a valid MAC address in EEPROM the host driver must set it. The host can also read, write and erase the EEPROM.
nTRST and nRESET are tied high when unused; TCK is pulled high through 10 kΩ. TEST1 and TEST4 are left open, TEST2 goes to VSS and TEST3 to VDD33IO.
Pull-ups and pull-downs are about 50 μA and are on unless a pin says otherwise. They only keep idle inputs defined; anything outside the chip that needs a pull needs its own resistor.
USBDP and USBDM timing follows the USB 2.0 specification.
Without external protection the part withstands ±8 kV HBM, ±8 kV IEC61000-4-2 contact and ±15 kV IEC61000-4-2 air-gap discharge.
Drivers exist for Windows 2000/XP/Vista, Linux, Windows CE and Mac OS, with an EEPROM utility.
